sections.title: The letters th
paragraphs: The letter pair th is spoken as the sound /θ/. Its main sound appears in the word (think) /θɪŋk/, which means to think. These two letters together make three different sounds.

sections.title: How to say th
paragraphs: Place the tip of your tongue lightly between your teeth. Blow air through the small gap without your voice. For the next sound, keep the exact same tongue position, but turn on your voice. Put a hand on your throat to feel the strong vibration. For the last sound, tap your tongue against the ridge behind your upper teeth.

sections.title: Spelling rules for th
paragraphs: The letters th make the sound /θ/ in most nouns, verbs and adjectives, like (thing) /θɪŋ/. You also hear this sound at the end of words, like (bath) /bɑːθ/. The letters make the sound /ð/ in grammatical words, like (this) /ðɪs/. They make that voiced sound between vowels, like (father) /fɑː.ðə/. In a few special words, they make the sound /t/, like (thyme) /taɪm/.

sections.title: Common mistakes with th
paragraphs: Do not replace the soft sound with the sound /s/ or /f/. Keep your tongue between your teeth so air slips through gently. Do not swap the voiced sound for the sound /d/ or /z/. If you hold your tongue behind your teeth, you will make the wrong sound.
